rules.title: Odds conversions are exact and reproducible
rules.description: Where a price is recorded in more than one notation, the notations agree: the American or fractional form converts to the recorded decimal odds.
rules.rationale: A price recorded in two notations that disagree is a price nobody can act on, and the discrepancy usually means one of them was typed rather than observed.
rules.remediation: Recompute the decimal odds from the quoted form, or correct the quoted form to match what the book displayed.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance that the notations are mutually consistent. It does not establish that either was the price the book was actually showing.

rules.title: Every quoted price carries its source and the moment it was observed
rules.description: Each recorded price names the book it came from and the timestamp at which it was observed, and the selection wagered on appears in the recorded market.
rules.rationale: A price is a fact about a moment. Without the book and the moment, a quote cannot be shown to have been current, and a wager cannot be traced to anything that was on offer.
rules.remediation: Record the book and the capture timestamp with every price, and include the selection in the recorded market.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance that provenance fields are present and internally consistent. Whether the recorded book was showing that price at that moment is outside what any record can establish.

rules.title: Odds are never fabricated
rules.description: No price is invented, estimated, or filled in from memory. Every price in a decision record was observed at a named book at a recorded time, and the price wagered on matches the market recorded beside it.
rules.rationale: Every downstream number — implied probability, edge, expected value, stake — is computed from the price. A fabricated price does not produce a slightly wrong answer; it produces a confident answer about a wager that was never on offer.
rules.remediation: Remove the record or replace the price with an observed quote and re-derive every value from it. Do not estimate a price that was not seen.
rules.$assuranceNote: Detects only the structural traces of fabrication: a price with no provenance, or one that disagrees with the market recorded alongside it. A plausible invented price with complete provenance fields is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a real one to this check. It MUST NOT be reported as 'no odds were fabricated'.
